system_prompt: You are a careful game QA test designer. Return ONLY valid JSON. Generate executable test specifications, not test results. Never claim a test passed. SCOPE: CONTROLS ONLY. You test whether each player control works, NOT whether the game can be won, scored, lost or completed. Work in two steps. STEP 1: read the play manual and plan and list every player control (a key the player presses), what it does, and the exact console line the manual says the game prints when it takes effect. STEP 2: write exactly one test per control: start the game, wait if the control needs a moment to be valid, press that key, wait about 1 second, and expect that exact console line. Do not test game mechanics, scoring, collisions, enemies, win/lose conditions, visuals or level completion: leave those requirements out entirely.

user_payload.task: Generate a versioned test suite specification for this game. Return JSON matching the requested shape.

requirements.text: The game must be a one-screen platformer.
requirements.check: The game window displays a single continuous level without scrolling or scene transitions.

requirements.text: A small character runs automatically to the right at a constant speed.
requirements.check: The character sprite moves horizontally to the right without player input, at a consistent pixel speed.
requirements.quote: a small character runs automatically to the right at a constant speed

requirements.text: The character runs across a series of platforms fixed to both the floor and the ceiling.
requirements.check: Platforms are visible at the bottom and top of the screen, and the character can move along them.
requirements.quote: across a series of platforms fixed to both the floor and the ceiling

requirements.text: Pressing Space instantly flips gravity, so the character falls toward the ceiling instead of the floor (or back to the floor if already flipped).
requirements.check: Pressing SPACE causes the character's vertical movement direction to reverse, and its orientation to flip.
requirements.quote: Pressing Space instantly flips gravity, so the character falls toward the ceiling instead of the floor (or back to the floor if already flipped)

requirements.text: The character smoothly reorients when gravity flips.
requirements.check: When gravity flips, the character sprite rotates smoothly to align with the new 'down' direction.
requirements.quote: smoothly reorienting which platforms it can land on

requirements.text: The character must stay on a platform; falling into empty space between platforms ends the run.
requirements.check: If the character is not colliding with a platform after a gravity flip or movement, the game state transitions to 'GAME OVER'.
requirements.quote: The character must stay on a platform; falling into empty space between platforms (after a flip or a missed landing) ends the run.

requirements.text: Passing each platform without falling adds 1 point.
requirements.check: The score increases by 1 each time the character successfully traverses a platform segment.
requirements.quote: Passing each platform without falling adds 1 point.

requirements.text: Show the score in the top-left corner at all times.
requirements.check: A numerical score display is continuously visible in the top-left corner of the screen.
requirements.quote: Show the score in the top-left corner at all times.

requirements.text: When the character falls off, show GAME OVER and the final score, and stop the run.
requirements.check: Upon falling, 'GAME OVER' text appears, the final score is displayed, and character movement ceases.
requirements.quote: When the character falls off, show GAME OVER and the final score, and stop the run.

requirements.text: Press R to restart with score 0 and the character back at the start.
requirements.check: Pressing R resets the score to 0, places the character at the initial starting position, and resumes automatic movement.
requirements.quote: Press R to restart with score 0 and the character back at the start.

requirements.check: Pressing ESCAPE closes the game window.

requirements.text: Print 'FLIP GRAVITY' to the console every time a gravity flip control takes effect.
requirements.check: The console outputs 'FLIP GRAVITY' each time the SPACE key is pressed and gravity changes.
requirements.quote: Print a line to the console every time a control takes effect: FLIP GRAVITY

requirements.text: Print 'RESTART' to the console every time a restart control takes effect.
requirements.check: The console outputs 'RESTART' each time the R key is pressed.
requirements.quote: Print a line to the console every time a control takes effect: RESTART

requirements.text: Print 'QUIT' to the console every time a quit control takes effect.
requirements.check: The console outputs 'QUIT' each time the ESCAPE key is pressed.
requirements.quote: Print a line to the console every time a control takes effect: QUIT

requirements.text: Print 'GAME OVER' to the console when the run ends.
requirements.check: The console outputs 'GAME OVER' when the character falls off a platform.
requirements.quote: and print GAME OVER when the run ends.

play_manual.test_input: Press SPACE to flip gravity when needed. Press R to restart after GAME OVER. Press ESCAPE to quit.
play_manual.expected_win_output: No WIN condition in this game; runs end with GAME OVER when the player falls.
play_manual.expected_lose_output:
The console will show lines such as:
FLIP GRAVITY
RESTART
QUIT
GAME OVER
(Score prints appear in the HUD; final "GAME OVER" is printed when the run ends.)
play_manual.notes:
Controls (and exact console prints):
- SPACE: flips gravity (prints exactly 'FLIP GRAVITY')
- R: restarts the run (prints exactly 'RESTART')
- ESCAPE: quits the game (prints exactly 'QUIT')
- When the character falls off the platforms the game prints 'GAME OVER'.
Implementation files and responsibilities:
- game/main.tscn: the main scene (GameManager, Player, Platforms, HUD nodes).
- game/game_manager.gd: Game state ownership (playing/game_over), input bindings, scoring, restart, HUD updates, connects to Player signals and prints control events.
- game/player.gd: automatic rightward movement, gravity flip logic and smooth rotation, collision detection against Platform instances, emits 'passed_platform' and 'fell'.
- game/platform.gd: platform geometry, drawing, collision shape, 'scored' flag and helpers get_rect()/get_right_edge().
Known limitations and approximations:
- No audio is implemented, per plan.
- Platforms are static rectangular nodes drawn procedurally; collision is created with StaticBody2D/CollisionShape2D to match visuals.
- The game has no victory condition; play ends on falling (GAME OVER).
- Restart always resets gravity to 'down' and rotation to 0 degrees (consistent restart behavior).
- Sprite scaling assumes the provided 32x32 PNG; if texture fails to load the player still functions but appears invisible.
Test notes:
- The viewport is fixed at 800x600. The Score label is at top-left. The Game Over label appears at top area when run ends.
- All required input actions are added at runtime by GameManager._ready().

controls.manual_quote: the exact manual sentence that states this key and its printed line

observation.target: the console line the play manual says this control prints

generation_notes: which controls were found, and any control that could not be tested and why

constraints: Fill 'controls' first (STEP 1), then 'tests' (STEP 2). One test per control, test_ids C01, C02, ...
Only list a control if the play manual names the key AND the exact console line it prints. Put the supporting manual sentence in manual_quote. Never invent a printed line.
Each test's 'expected' must be exactly the control's 'prints' line, and observation.method must be stdout.
For a terminal (text) game a control is a typed command: use {"type": "input", "text": "go north"} (the validator adds the Enter) and put the command in the control's key field.

Actions: press / key_down / key_up / wait (and input for terminal games) only. Key names are pyautogui names: up, down, left, right, space, enter, esc, and single letters (r, w, a, s, d...). A wait uses 'seconds' (max 30).

If the manual says a control only works in a certain state (e.g. R only after game over, jump only when on the ground), add the inputs/waits needed to reach that state first. If that state cannot be reached reliably with simple inputs, mark the test not_testable and say why.
Set requirement_index to the plan requirement that mentions this control (zero-based); if none fits, use 0.
Do not write code, do not invent script_path values (use null), and do not add tests for anything other than controls.
